claims.claim: Coulomb energy dominates over LJ in random charges system
claims.evidence: E_coulomb mean = -119.18 eV vs E_LJ mean = 0.003 eV

claims.claim: Long-range component accounts for 75-93% of Coulomb energy at typical cutoffs
claims.evidence: Ewald decomposition: at α=0.2, LR fraction = 77.7%; at α=0.5, LR fraction = 92.6%

claims.claim: Charged dimer binding curve follows 1/r Coulomb law at large separations
claims.evidence: Coulomb fit yields E_inf=0.600 eV, q_eff=1.373 eV·Å with good agreement beyond 6 Å

claims.claim: Significant Coulomb energy persists beyond 10 Å cutoff
claims.evidence: At 10 Å cutoff, Coulomb contribution = 0.137 eV

claims.claim: Ag3 +1 and -1 charge states have identical PES
claims.evidence: Position, energy, and force differences are exactly zero for all 60 frames

claims.claim: Short-range models cannot distinguish Ag3 charge states
claims.evidence: With identical geometry and energy, any model based on local features gives identical predictions

claims.claim: 4G-HDNNP achieves 3 orders of magnitude improvement over 2G-HDNNP for Ag3
claims.evidence: From Ko et al. (2021): 2G errors 0.605/2.017 eV/atom vs 4G errors 1.166/0.320 meV/atom
